mainTopic: Animals and money a woman set aside for her נזירות offerings after her husband cancels her נדר, and whether a husband owes his wife her offerings
overview: The amud opens with the last line of the previous אגדה: לוט's older daughter was rewarded when her descendants, through רות, reached kingship four generations before her sister's. Then a new משנה begins. A woman vowed to be a נזירה and set aside animals for her offerings, but her husband then cancelled (הפרה) her נדר. If the animal belonged to him, it goes back to the flock as an ordinary animal. If it was hers, the חטאת is left to die, the עולה is offered as an עולה, and the שלמים is offered as שלמים, eaten for one day and without bread. Money she had not assigned goes to voluntary offerings. Assigned money follows its offering: the חטאת money is destroyed, while the עולה and שלמים money buys those offerings. The גמרא then asks which תנא holds that a husband does not owe his wife her offerings. רב חסדא says the רבנן, because רבי יהודה makes the husband responsible through the כתובה. רבא answers that even רבי יהודה only obligates him for what she needs, and in a second version רב חסדא himself says the משנה is רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The older daughter's reward: four generations of kingship first
steps.stepSummary: The previous אגדה ends: the older daughter of לוט merited that her descendants reached Jewish kingship four generations before the younger daughter's.
steps.simpleTranslation: She merited to come first, by four generations, to kingship in Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the story from the previous section about לוט's daughters. It says the older daughter's family, through רות, reached the throne four generations earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The older daughter is the mother of מואב, and from מואב came רות. Her line reached kingship with דוד's family four generations before the younger daughter's line (עמון, through נעמה, mother of רחבעם). So her rushing to act was paid back with an earlier reward.

keyTerms.meaning: She merited / earned
She came first / preceded
Generations
Kingship / the monarchy

steps.whatToRemember: The older daughter of לוט was rewarded by having her descendants rule first, four generations ahead of her sister's.

phrases.english: She merited and preceded by four generations
phrases.notes: "She" is לוט's older daughter, the mother of מואב, from whom רות came.

phrases.english: to the kingship in Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: זָכְתָה וְקָדְמָה אַרְבָּעָה דּוֹרוֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לַמַּלְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the אגדה from the previous section of the דף.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The older daughter's line, through רות, reached kingship four generations before the younger daughter's line.

steps.title: New משנה: wife's נזיר vow cancelled after she set aside an animal that was her husband's
steps.stepSummary: A woman vowed נזירות and set aside an animal for her offerings, then her husband cancelled the vow. If the animal belonged to him, it simply goes back to graze with the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman vowed to be a נזירה and set aside her animal, and then her husband cancelled her vow. If the animal was his, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a case: a woman set aside an animal for her נזירות offerings, but her husband then cancelled her vow. The first ruling covers an animal that actually belonged to the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the husband cancels the vow, she is no longer a נזירה and has no offerings to bring. If the animal was his, it goes back into the flock and is treated as an ordinary animal. The more complicated rulings, for an animal that was her own, come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the opening of a new משנה)
A person who vowed to avoid wine, haircuts and contact with the dead
She set aside (designated for an offering)
He cancelled (a husband nullifying his wife's vow)
Flock

steps.confusionAlert: "Her animal" in the first line just means the animal she set aside. The משנה then asks who really owned it, him or her, and the ruling depends on that.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman who vowed to be a nazirite,
and separated her animal,
and afterward her husband nullified it for her.
If the animal was his —
it shall go out and graze in the flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה with a new הלכה topic, unrelated to the אגדה before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the woman's vow was cancelled and the animal belonged to the husband, it returns to the flock as an ordinary animal.

steps.title: If the animal was hers: what happens to each type of offering
steps.stepSummary: If the animal was the woman's own, each offering gets its own ruling. The חטאת is left to die, the עולה is offered as an עולה, and the שלמים is offered as שלמים, eaten for one day and without bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the animal was hers: the חטאת must die, the עולה is brought as an עולה, and the שלמים is brought as שלמים. These are eaten for one day and do not need bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the same case for an animal the woman owned herself. It gives a separate ruling for each of the three נזיר offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עולה and a שלמים can be brought as voluntary offerings, so those animals are still offered. A חטאת cannot be brought by choice, so it is left to die. The שלמים keeps one feature of a נזיר's שלמים (eaten for only one day) but drops another (no bread loaves).

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering
It must die (left to die, not offered)
Burnt-offering, fully burned on the מזבח
Peace-offering, mostly eaten by the owners
Require bread (the loaves and wafers brought with a נזיר's שלמים)

steps.confusionAlert: A regular שלמים may be eaten for two days. Here it is eaten for only one day, like a נזיר's שלמים, even though she is no longer a נזירה.

phrases.english: And if the animal was hers,
the sin-offering — must die,
and the burnt-offering — is sacrificed as a burnt-offering,
the peace-offering — is sacrificed as a peace-offering,
and they are eaten for one day,
and they do not require bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other half of the case: the animal belonged to the woman rather than the husband.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Her own animals: the חטאת is left to die, the עולה is offered as an עולה, and the שלמים is offered as שלמים, eaten for one day and without bread.

steps.title: What happens to money she set aside for the offerings
steps.stepSummary: Money she set aside without assigning it to a specific offering goes to voluntary communal offerings. Money assigned to the חטאת must be destroyed. One may not benefit from it, but there is no מעילה for using it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she had unassigned money, it goes to voluntary offerings. If the money was assigned, the money for the חטאת goes to the Dead Sea. One may not benefit from it, but one does not commit מעילה with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from animals to money the woman set aside for her offerings. The ruling depends on whether she assigned the coins to specific offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unassigned money is not tied to the חטאת in particular, so all of it can go to voluntary offerings. Money clearly assigned to the חטאת is treated like the חטאת animal itself and must be destroyed. It still has some holiness, so no one may use it, yet someone who does use it is not liable for מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Unassigned money: set aside for the offerings without saying which coins are for which
Voluntary offerings (here, communal ones)
Assigned money: each sum designated for a specific offering
The Dead Sea, meaning the money must be destroyed
Commit מעילה (misuse of הקדש property, which requires an offering)

steps.whatToRemember: Unassigned money goes to voluntary offerings. Money assigned to the חטאת is destroyed, like the חטאת animal: it is forbidden to use, but there is no מעילה liability.
steps.confusionAlert: "Not benefit" and "not misuse" are not the same thing. Using this money is forbidden, but it does not bring the formal penalty of מעילה.

phrases.english: If she had unallocated funds —
they go to gift offerings.
Allocated funds, the money for the sin-offering —
go to the Dead Sea.
phrases.notes: This is a way of saying the money must be destroyed so no one uses it.

phrases.english: One may not benefit from them, but one does not commit misuse with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same case to money instead of animals.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unassigned money goes to voluntary offerings. Money assigned to the חטאת must be destroyed: benefit from it is forbidden, but there is no מעילה.

steps.title: Money set aside for the עולה and for the שלמים
steps.stepSummary: Money set aside for her עולה is used to bring an עולה, and there is מעילה for using it. Money set aside for her שלמים is used to bring a שלמים, which is eaten for one day and has no bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Money for the עולה: they bring an עולה with it, and one who uses it for himself commits מעילה. Money for the שלמים: they bring a שלמים with it. It is eaten for one day and does not need loaves of bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of what happens to her money once her husband cancels the vow. Here it covers money set aside specifically for the עולה and for the שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each pot of money follows the offering it was set aside for, just like the animals did in step 3. Unlike the חטאת money in step 4, the עולה money is fully holy, so there is מעילה for using it. The שלמים keeps the same special limits as before: eaten for one day only and brought without bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Money set aside to buy an עולה (burnt offering)
One is liable for מעילה, the sin of using holy property for personal benefit
Eaten for one day only, not the usual two days of a שלמים
Does not need the loaves that normally come with a נזיר's שלמים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two money rules. Money for the חטאת (step 4) has no מעילה, but money for the עולה does have מעילה.

phrases.english: The money for the burnt offering —
they bring a burnt offering, and one is liable for misuse of it.
The money for the peace offering —
they bring a peace offering, and it is eaten for one day,
and it does not require bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the משנה's list of rulings about money she set aside, after the rules for unassigned money and חטאת money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Money for the עולה buys an עולה and carries מעילה. Money for the שלמים buys a שלמים eaten for one day without bread.

steps.title: Who holds that a husband does not owe his wife her offerings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the משנה's view that a husband is not obligated to provide his wife's offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who is the תנא who taught that a husband is not obligated to her?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by asking whose opinion the משנה follows. This sets up רב חסדא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that if the animal was the husband's, it simply goes back to the flock (step 2). That ruling assumes she had no right to his animal for her offering, meaning he does not owe her offerings. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that follows and explains the משנה
Who is the תנא (sage of the משנה period) who taught this?
Is obligated / owes, like someone under a debt

phrases.english: GEMARA
Who is the tanna
who holds that a husband is not obligated to her?
phrases.notes: He means obligated to supply her required offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן תְּנָא דְּבַעַל לָא מִשְׁתַּעְבַּד לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה into the גמרא, asking about an assumption hidden in the ruling of step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a husband is not obligated to provide his wife's offerings, as the משנה assumes.

steps.title: רב חסדא: The משנה follows the רבנן, not רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the משנה follows the רבנן. According to רבי יהודה, the husband owes her offerings, so his animal would not just go back to the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is the רבנן. Because if you thought it was רבי יהודה, why should the animal go out and graze in the flock? He is obligated to her!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers the question: the משנה is the view of the רבנן. He proves it by showing the משנה could not fit רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the husband owes her offerings, as רבי יהודה holds, then her setting aside his animal would count, and it would stay holy. Since the משנה says the husband's animal just returns to the flock, it must hold that he owes her nothing. That is the view of the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority opinion against an individual sage
If it should enter your mind, introducing an idea that will be rejected
It goes out and grazes in the flock, meaning it is not holy at all

phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said:
It is the opinion of the Rabbis.
For if it should enter your mind
that it is Rabbi Yehuda,
why should it go out and graze in the flock?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's ruling about the husband's animal from step 2.

phrases.english: After all, he is obligated to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows the רבנן, because according to רבי יהודה the husband owes her offerings and his animal would stay holy.

steps.title: The source for רבי יהודה: a husband brings his wife's offerings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה holds a husband brings a rich person's offering for his wife, and all her required offerings. The reason is that in the כתובה he takes on all her earlier obligations.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says: A man brings a rich person's offering for his wife. And the same goes for all the offerings she is obligated to bring, because he wrote to her: 'All responsibility that you have upon me from before this.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי יהודה really holds the husband owes his wife's offerings. This backs up רב חסדא's reasoning in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה says a wealthy husband must bring the more expensive 'rich' version of an offering for his wife. This covers all her offerings, even obligations from before the marriage. The reason is a line in the כתובה where he accepts responsibility for all her earlier obligations.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering of a rich person, the costlier version of a sliding-scale offering
Responsibility, a guarantee to cover obligations
The marriage contract, the husband's written obligations to his wife

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב חסדא, the משנה follows the רבנן: a husband does not owe his wife her offerings. רבי יהודה disagrees, because in the כתובה the husband takes on all her obligations, including offerings. רבא disagrees with רב חסדא in the next step, and in a second version (step 10) רב חסדא himself says the משנה is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
A man brings the offering of a rich person
phrases.notes: Some offerings depend on wealth, like a woman's offering after childbirth. If he is rich, he brings the rich version for her.

phrases.english: on behalf of his wife.
And so too all her offerings
that she is obligated to bring,
for this is what he wrote to her:
'All responsibility that you have upon me
from before this.'
phrases.notes: This is the husband's line in the כתובה. Literally, 'from before this,' meaning from before the marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אָדָם מֵבִיא קׇרְבַּן עָשִׁיר עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim about רבי יהודה that רב חסדא relied on in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that according to רבי יהודה a husband is obligated to provide his wife's offerings.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה rules that a husband brings a rich person's offering and all her required offerings, based on the כתובה clause.

steps.title: רבא: The משנה can fit even רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רב חסדא. Even רבי יהודה only makes the husband pay for offerings his wife actually needs. Once he cancels her vow, she needs no offering, so his animal goes back to the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי יהודה. When is the husband obligated to her? Only for something she needs. For something she does not need, he is not obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer to the question of which תנא the משנה follows. He says it can match רבי יהודה too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא thought רבי יהודה's rule (the husband pays all her offerings) clashes with the משנה. רבא limits that rule: the husband's debt only covers offerings she truly needs. After he cancels her נזירות she has no offering to bring, so even רבי יהודה agrees the animal is not owed to her.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. This introduces a way to fit a source with an opinion we thought it argued against.
He is obligated (literally 'bound') to her
Something she needs

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יהודה's rule from the כתובה has a limit. It covers real needs, not offerings that are no longer required.

phrases.english: Rava said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,
when he is obligated to her —
it is for something she needs,
for something she does not need — no.
phrases.notes: Once he cancelled her vow, she no longer needs the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question in step 6, against רב חסדא's answer in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה can follow רבי יהודה, because the husband only owes offerings his wife actually needs.

steps.title: Second version: רב חסדא says the משנה is רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: In a second version of the discussion, רב חסדא says the משנה follows רבי יהודה. The husband owes only what she needs. According to the רבנן he owes her nothing at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Who is the תנא? רב חסדא said: It is רבי יהודה. When is the husband obligated to her? For something she needs. For something she does not need, he is not. For if it were the רבנן, he would not be obligated to her at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the same discussion. In this version רב חסדא himself says the משנה is רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה suggests that the husband would sometimes be responsible for her offering, but not after he cancels her vow. That fits רבי יהודה, who obligates him only for what she needs. The רבנן never obligate him at all, so the משנה's case does not seem to fit them.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not obligated to her at all

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first version (step 7) רב חסדא said the משנה is the רבנן. In this second version he says it is רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Some say:
Who is the tanna?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא.
phrases.english: Rav Ḥisda said: It is Rabbi Yehuda.
And when he is obligated to her —
it is for something she needs,
for something she does not need — no.
For if it were the Rabbis —
he is not obligated to her at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: מַאן תַּנָּא? אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second version of the discussion from steps 6-7, in which רב חסדא reaches the opposite answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is behind the משנה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, because only he makes the husband responsible, and only for offerings she needs.

steps.title: Why the משנה cannot follow the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: According to the רבנן, the only way the husband could be responsible is if he gave the animal to her. But then it is simply her own animal, which is not the משנה's case of 'his' animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what is the case where he is obligated to her according to the רבנן? For example, if he transferred the animal to her. But once he transferred it to her, it is her own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the second version by ruling out the רבנן. It asks how a husband could ever be responsible for her offering according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only possible case for the רבנן is that he gave the animal to her as a gift. Then the animal belongs to her, and the משנה's rule about his own animal going back to the flock would not apply. So the משנה must follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (literally 'how is it like?')
He transferred it into her ownership
Her own

steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, the משנה follows רבי יהודה. A husband owes his wife's offerings only when she needs them. The רבנן never obligate him, and if he gives her the animal it is simply hers.

phrases.english: Rather, what is the case where he is obligated to her —
for example, where he transferred it to her,
but since he transferred it to her —
it is her own.
phrases.notes: Then it counts as her animal, not his, so it does not fit the משנה's case of his animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the claim in step 10 that the משנה cannot follow the רבנן
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה follows רבי יהודה and not the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: Reasoning: for the רבנן, the only case where he is responsible is where he gave her the animal, and then it is simply hers.
